title: Prefill/Decode Disaggregation
summary: LLM inference has two phases with different bottlenecks: prefill (compute-heavy prompt processing) and decode (memory-bandwidth heavy token generation). Disaggregating them onto specialized pools can raise utilization — at the cost of KV transfer complexity.

sections.title: Two phases, two bottlenecks
paragraphs: Prefill processes the prompt in parallel-friendly matmuls — often compute bound. Decode generates one token at a time while reading a growing KV cache — often memory-bandwidth bound.
A single mixed batch forces GPUs to compromise. Long prompts stall short interactive decodes and vice versa.

sections.title: Disaggregation idea
paragraphs: Run prefill on compute-optimized nodes; ship KV cache (or references) to decode nodes optimized for bandwidth and concurrency. Schedulers route based on phase.
The hard part is KV transfer latency, memory ownership, and failure handling mid-request.

sections.title: When it pays off
paragraphs: Workloads with long prompts and moderate output lengths, or highly variable mixes, benefit most. Short prompt/short output chat may not justify the complexity.
Measure GPU goodput, KV bytes moved, and p99 end-to-end — not just theoretical FLOPs.

sections.title: Design checklist
paragraphs: Define SLOs separately for time-to-first-token and inter-token latency. Autoscaling signals should include KV memory and queue time per phase.

deepDive.title: Prefill/Decode Disaggregation — Operations
paragraphs: Operating Prefill/Decode Disaggregation in production means defining SLIs before tuning knobs, knowing amplification costs, and rehearsing failure modes.
Prefer reversible changes, feature flags, and canaries. Measure p50/p99 and error rate under load that matches production skew.
bullets: Define capacity from the scarcest resource
Keep rollback cheaper than forward repair when possible

deepDive.title: Prefill/Decode Disaggregation — Failure modes
paragraphs: Common failures around Prefill/Decode Disaggregation include overload, partial dependency outages, and silent correctness bugs that pass happy-path tests.
Inject faults in staging: latency, loss, clock skew, and disk full. Verify alerts fire and degradation is intentional.

expert.title: Prefill/Decode Disaggregation — Expert notes
paragraphs: At the expert level, Prefill/Decode Disaggregation intersects multi-region consistency, cost envelopes, and organizational constraints (team ownership, on-call load).
Write down the non-goals. Many outages come from optimizing a metric that was never the product requirement.

practices: Split SLOs for TTFT and decode rate
Benchmark KV transfer overhead before committing

keyTakeaways: Prefill and decode stress hardware differently
KV movement is the central design cost
whyItMatters: Inference cost curves at scale are dominated by phase mix. Architects who treat 'LLM serving' as one uniform stage will mis-size fleets.
reflectionQuestions: What is your traffic's prompt length vs output length distribution?
numbersToKnow: Know your p99 latency budget before adding hops
Peak load ≠ average load — plan headroom (often 2–3×)
Cross-region RTT is often ~50–150ms one way
